body: Please try handling this argument via `clap::ValueEnum`.
I think at this time I would prefer `include_bytes!`, but this is acceptable.

I actually meant handling the validation via a type that manually implement the `clap::ValueEnum` trait, by looking at the values in `Presets`, instead of the manual validation you had before.
If the implementation does require presets to be added to the code manually, please don't use `rust-embed` and update `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

I am quite new to Rust so there might be another way around. The only way I can think of implementing `fn value_variants<'a>() -> &'a [Self]` method without explicitly listing all the options would be to create a procedural macro. As far as I understand, proc macros require a separate crate to maintain, which would be an unreasonable thing to do for this small feature.

I liked the idea of not listing presets manually, but if my understanding is correct, I will rewrite it using `include_bytes!`.
I don't think it needs to be an enum, `struct Preset(String)` should work without macros.

I've tried implementing it this way, the problem that I have is a lifetime of a slice. If I create it's value in runtime inside `value_variants`, then it's lifetime is limited to this function and thus I can't return it. So it has to be a compile time constant
Could `struct Preset(&'static str)` work? Or maybe integer indices?

That solves part of the problem. The other part is where `&[Preset]` will be borrowed from. The only thing I can think of (other than macro generating literal) is using something like `static mut PRESETS: Vec<Preset> = Vec::new() `, changing it in the method and returning it's slice, but that requires `unsafe` block and overall feels ugly
`OnceCell` or `Box::leak` might work in that case, but that's not ideal. It might be possible to generate a rust file in `build.rs` with the files and required definitions?
I think it should be possible, I will look into it
I'd prefer just using a `match` instead of a `HashMap` here. And instead of `String`, please just print the bytes as-is.
For these statements, perhaps use the names directly (`{presets}` instead of `{}`) instead of arguments to make this more readable. Also, `format!` and `writeln!` are redundant here.
`lib.rs` already has this. Please try re-using it.

`expect` makes for poor error messages (the other instances in this PR should never be hit, so they should be fine). I think doing nothing is preferable here, as printing an error message when something like `head` is used is unexpected. (#885)

```suggestion
        let _ = stdout.write_all(include_bytes!(r"{full_path}"));
```
